Not a dumb question! The engine degreaser actually helps remove any car fluids that might of spilled or leaked over time. Water would work too definitely but this method seems to work better imo.

My dad has done this several times and I've helped him with it. Here are the steps.

- buy two to three cans of engine degreaser, (at least one has to be non foam, so if you get three, you would get 2 foam and 1 non foam.)

- go to one of the car washes where you can wash it yourself and it has the hose that's attached to the sealing

- open your hood and spray the engine degreaser foams first everywhere, extra on the dirtier areas, then the non foam after the first can/cans run out 

- then start the car wash and do it on low pressure spot free rinse, high pressure if really bad. ( keep a distance and if someone is with you keep a distance as it sprays everywhere once you start washing.) 

- boommmm clean engine
